subject: Spike backstop, rebate framing & threshold alignment
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan@craftly.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected spike this morning — options for headroom?

Vanessa,

Quick context: we saw a 6x spike in generation volume between 07:30–08:15 PT as a model rollout amplified traffic. The app stayed up but we hit our quota and started seeing 429s in a couple regions. Attached is a short usage snapshot and a couple logs.

We need to understand short-term options to avoid hitting hard rate limits again during this runway window (we're in the middle of a marketing push). Can you outline:
- Temporary headroom (duration / cap) you can enable immediately
- Any pro-rated credit or rebate for the overrun window
- How this will appear on next invoice and whether it'll be tagged as a one-off true-up

We are sensitive to long-term commit changes — ideally a short emergency carve-out while we stabilize our rollout.

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
Product Ops, Craftly AI
attachments: craftly_usage_snapshot_20261108.csv (csv), billing_snapshot_nov.pdf (pdf)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@craftly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>; Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T10:04:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected spike this morning — options for headroom?

Ethan — thanks for the flag and the snapshot. Important that the app stayed healthy. Quick read: the spike looks API-heavy with many short requests (same model).

Suggested immediate path (short-term, minimal paperwork):
1) Activate a 72-hour temporary headroom of +300% on current QPS for the eu/us regions, capped at a hard token ceiling (we'll throttle to that ceiling if exceeded).
2) We'll treat the usage over your committed threshold as an "overrun" and propose a one-time reconciliation charge; to be fair, we're willing to apply a 30% rebate on the incremental overrun amount for this event if you accept the proposed amendment.
3) Add an invoice note and line item called "Emergency headroom (Nov 8–11) — provisional"; final true-up will appear on the Dec invoice after reconciliation.

Action items for you: confirm you want the 72-hour headroom and whether procurement needs a doc/PO. If yes, I'll raise the amendment (attached template) and loop finance for approval.

CCing Ben for ops implications and Lauren for billing/credit approval.

-Vanessa
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_amendment_v1.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>; Ethan Cole <ethan@craftly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:07:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected spike this morning — options for headroom?

Agree with Vanessa's approach. A couple operational clarifications from infra:
- We'll enable the headroom within 30 minutes of receiving confirmation from Craftly (manual toggle).
- Implement a hard token ceiling at X tokens/min (ops will confirm exact number when they flip the toggle).
- We'll emit a detailed usage export for the event (hourly granularity) to support procurement and audit.

From a risk standpoint I recommend we mark this as an "ephemeral exception":
- Headroom window limited to 72 hours, non-recurring without explicit contract change.
- If this event repeats, recommend converting to a short-term burst package or temporary commit uplift.

Happy to proceed once Ethan confirms.

—Ben
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan@craftly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T13:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected spike this morning — options for headroom?

Finance notes / approval pathway:
- We can approve a provisional 30% rebate on the incremental overrun as Vanessa proposed, but we need Craftly to:
  1) Sign the short amendment (DocuSign link below) that documents the headroom window and rebate terms.
  2) Confirm the billing contact + PO number if they want the charge invoiced to a PO.
- The provisional credit will be applied only after we receive the event usage export and perform reconciliation (expected 7–10 business days).

DocuSign for amendment: https://docusign.net/US-1234-5678/contract-amendment
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1245789/DEAL-2026-0792

If Procurement needs a more formal appendix (SOW-style), we can convert the amendment to an appendix and include the hourly usage export as schedule A.

-Lauren
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@craftly.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>; Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan@craftly.ai>; Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Unexpected spike this morning — options for headroom?

Vanessa / Lauren — thanks for the clear path. Craftly confirms we want the 72-hour headroom and the rebate framing. Next steps from our side:
- We'll route the amendment through procurement today. PO number will be supplied (expected within 24 hours).
- Please attach the hourly usage export and the proposed amendment (docx) to the DocuSign envelope so legal has the event evidence.
- One ask: can you drop a short explanatory blurb for legal that states the rebate is a one-time concession tied specifically to the Nov 8 spike and does not change our underlying committed tiers? A single paragraph would be perfect.

If that works, we'll sign and return.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Craftly AI
attachments: none.
